correctness.rationale: For an interval centered at a, the trial quadratic P=(t−a)(t−b) is u(u+a−b) in the centered coordinate u. The odd cross term integrates to zero and the two even integrals are ℓ³/12 and ℓ⁵/80; the other interval is identical with a,b exchanged. The full norm D of this monic quadratic is at least 1/180 by shifted Legendre orthogonality. With a,b=1/2+s±h its norm is 1/80+s²/2−h²/6+(s²−h²)². At fixed h²≤1/4 it is minimized at s=0, and the ratio 4z/(z²−z/6+1/80) with z=h² has derivative of sign 1/80−z². Its unique maximum is 30+18√5 at z=1/(4√5), with s=0, giving the stated unique unordered pair. The normalized trial bound and ∑ℓ_i^r≤q^r give the all-q bound with 9/4 on q⁵. For lengths q²,q−q² at the two fixed centers, the shifted orthonormal Legendre Gram matrix compresses to A≽c q² I on the two point-evaluation span: the leading weighted evaluations are independent and symmetric integration changes their compression by O(q³). Its mixed block with the orthogonal unit trial vector is O(q³), and that vector's diagonal quotient d is Cq³+O(q⁴). Since λ_min≤d≪λ_min(A), the Schur correction is bounded by O(q⁶)/Ω(q²)=O(q⁴), yielding the matching lower asymptotic. The unrelaxed upper bound has the product of the center ratio and the fractional cubic-length sum; compactness and uniqueness force the specified unordered centers and min(ℓ_i)/q→0. This is necessity only, not a claim that every vanishing fraction suffices, nor that the short band must lie on a fixed side. The single-band trial gives O(q⁵); rescaling a centered one to a fixed interval and using degree-two norm equivalence also gives a matching Ω(q⁵) for that band. Complex coefficients do not change the real symmetric Gram eigenvalues, and t=|z|² pushes probability area to dt. Reviewed the submitted script and recorded numerical output without executing the script; the decisive checks above are analytic for the claimed regimes.
